# Dirtycoin

> Dirtycoin is a static website for USDC (United States Dirty Coin), a project coin on Solana,
> and for the Trenches Market: seven item coins traded on Pump.fun. The site has no backend,
> no database and no smart contract of its own. It reads public Solana state and links to
> Pump.fun; every trade is signed in the user's own wallet on Pump.fun.

This file is written for language models and for people who want to check how the project
works before they trade. Everything below can be verified on-chain or in Pump.fun's public
documentation.

## Naming

- "USDC" on this site is the project coin, United States Dirty Coin. It is not Circle's USDC
  stablecoin.
- In code the project coin is also called DC or $DC.

## Status

- USDC is not launched yet. It is planned on Pump.fun via `create_v2`, so its mint is a
  Token-2022 mint, paired with SOL, without mayhem mode.
- None of the seven item coins is launched yet. Their mints are `null` in the site's config
  until launch.
- Prices shown before launch are labelled `Preview` and are placeholders, not market data.

## How the market works

1. Each item (Glock 19, Weapon Case, Briefcase, ParaPactum, To The Moon Visa, Bitcoin,
   Ethereum) launches on Pump.fun as its own coin, quoted in USDC (a Pump.fun custom pair).
2. Buys and sells happen on the Pump.fun bonding curve. When the curve sells out it is marked
   complete and the coin trades on PumpSwap.
3. Trading activity in the seven item coins counts toward an NFT airdrop. There are no
   seasons. The owner computes it from public trade data in a snapshot; the formula and the
   snapshot date are not decided yet.

## Contracts

- Pump.fun program: `6EF8rrecthR5Dkzon8Nwu78hRvfCKubJ14M5uBEwF6P`.
- Bonding curve account: PDA with seeds `["bonding-curve", mint]` under that program.
- Fields the site reads: `virtual_token_reserves`, `virtual_quote_reserves`,
  `real_token_reserves`, `real_quote_reserves`, `token_total_supply`, `complete`,
  `quote_mint`, `creator_fee_bps`.
- Curve invariant: `virtual_quote_reserves × virtual_token_reserves = k`. Spot price is
  `virtual_quote_reserves / virtual_token_reserves`.
- After graduation the price comes from the PumpSwap pool:
  `effective_quote_reserves = quote_vault.amount + virtual_quote_reserves`.
- The creator fee of each item (`creator_fee_bps`) is set at launch and stored in the curve
  account, so anyone can read it. Its values are not decided yet.
- Sources: Pump.fun public docs and IDL at github.com/pump-fun/pump-public-docs
  (`docs/instructions/CREATE_WITH_PUMP_COIN_QUOTE.md`, `docs/instructions/TRADE_V3.md`,
  `idl/pump.json`).

## What the website does

- Reads every item's bonding curve in one `getMultipleAccounts` call over public Solana RPC
  and decodes it with the layout from the Pump IDL. An item whose curve is not quoted in the
  project coin is shown as unavailable, never with a price.
- Estimates a trade on the curve with exact integer math (before fees) and links to the
  item's Pump.fun page. It never builds, signs or sends a transaction.
- Reads the connected wallet's SOL and token balances. Wallet connection grants no spending
  rights; signing stays in the wallet.
- Shows a Battle Pass level derived from the wallet's SOL balance using a public, versioned
  ruleset (`/data/battle-pass.json`). A level shown by the site is not proof of anything;
  partners must verify on-chain.

## What the website does not do

- It holds no funds, keys or user data, and has no account database.
- It runs no analytics or ad trackers. Hosting, RPC and media providers still see IP
  addresses.
- It promises no yield, payout, profit or APR. Item prices move with trading on the curve.

## Next in the Trenches

A GameFi sector: games, a player-backed house, thousands of NFTs and an on-chain activity
feed. The home page previews it. Its chain, programs, supply and mechanics are in design.

## Risk

These are high-risk assets. By investing, you may lose your funds.
